name: Core: Automation and Programmability
description: 24 original questions for Automation and Programmability (10% of the v1.1 blueprint).
author: CCNA Academy

questions.stem: Match each activity to the network plane it belongs to.
questions.explanation: The data plane moves user traffic, the control plane builds forwarding information, and the management plane is used to operate the device.
questions.whyCorrect: Forwarding a frame using the MAC address table → Data plane; Exchanging OSPF LSAs with a neighbor → Control plane; An administrator logging in with SSH → Management plane
left: Forwarding a frame using the MAC address table
Exchanging OSPF LSAs with a neighbor
An administrator logging in with SSH

questions.stem: A Python script retrieves the device inventory from Catalyst Center using its REST API. Which interface is the script using?
questions.explanation: Picture the controller in the middle: applications above (northbound, usually REST/JSON) and devices below (southbound).
questions.tip: North = up to apps; south = down to devices.
questions.whyCorrect: Applications talk to the controller through its northbound API.
whyWrong: The controller uses southbound interfaces to talk to network devices.
The data plane forwards user traffic.
The underlay is the physical IP transport network.

questions.stem: Which of these are southbound protocols a controller can use to configure network devices? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Southbound options include NETCONF, RESTCONF, OpenFlow, OpFlex, SSH/CLI and SNMP.
questions.whyCorrect: NETCONF configures devices over SSH using YANG data models. OpenFlow programs forwarding tables on switches.
whyWrong: JSON is a data format, not a protocol.
YAML is a data format, typically used by Ansible playbooks.
OAuth is an authorization framework, typically for APIs.

questions.stem: True or false: In controller-based networking, user traffic no longer passes through switches; the controller forwards all packets.
questions.explanation: The controller centralizes control and management, but devices still forward user traffic in their data planes.
questions.whyCorrect: The statement is false. The controller centralizes control and management, but devices still forward user traffic in their data planes.
whyWrong: The statement is false, so this choice is incorrect.

questions.stem: Match each Cisco SD-Access function to the technology that provides it.
questions.explanation: SD-Access builds a fabric: an IS-IS underlay, VXLAN encapsulation, LISP mapping, and Catalyst Center for automation and assurance.
questions.whyCorrect: Underlay routing → IS-IS; Overlay data plane encapsulation → VXLAN; Overlay control plane → LISP; Management and automation → Catalyst Center

questions.stem: In a software-defined fabric, what is the underlay?
questions.explanation: Underlay = physical transport; overlay = virtual networks on top; fabric = both managed as one.
options: The virtual tunnels that carry user traffic
questions.whyCorrect: Overlay tunnels are built on top of it.
whyWrong: That is the overlay.
APIs are not part of the underlay.
The underlay covers the whole transport network.

questions.stem: Why does controller-based management reduce configuration errors across 300 switches?
questions.explanation: Automation improves consistency, speed and auditability, and frees engineers for design work.
options: Policy is defined centrally and pushed consistently
It removes the need for spanning tree
It disables the management plane on switches
questions.whyCorrect: Automation removes repetitive manual steps.
whyWrong: Controllers do not change Layer 2 loop prevention requirements.
Encryption is unrelated to consistency.
Devices still need management access.

questions.stem: A monitoring platform learns typical DHCP onboarding times for each site and alerts when a site deviates. Which kind of AI is this?
questions.explanation: Predictive AI uses telemetry to build baselines, detect anomalies and forecast problems.
questions.whyCorrect: It learns a baseline from historical data and flags deviations.
whyWrong: Generative AI creates content such as text or configurations.
A static threshold does not learn per-site baselines.
ACL logging records matches; it does not learn behavior.

questions.stem: An engineer uses a generative AI assistant to draft an ACL for a production router. What is the correct practice?
questions.explanation: Use AI to speed up drafting and analysis, but keep humans responsible for validating changes.
options: Validate it in a lab before deploying
Apply it immediately because AI output is always accurate
Trust it because the model was trained on vendor documentation
Paste the router's credentials into the prompt for better results
questions.whyCorrect: Generative output can be plausible but wrong.
whyWrong: Generated configurations can contain errors.
Training data does not guarantee correctness.
Sensitive data should not be shared with AI services.

questions.stem: True or false: Supervised machine learning trains models using labeled data.
questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labeled examples; unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data; reinforcement learning learns from rewards.
questions.whyCorrect: The statement is true. Supervised learning uses labeled examples; unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data; reinforcement learning learns from rewards.
whyWrong: The statement is true, so this choice is incorrect.

questions.stem: Match each CRUD operation to the HTTP method normally used in REST APIs.
questions.explanation: REST maps CRUD to HTTP verbs. PATCH is used for partial updates.
questions.whyCorrect: Create → POST; Read → GET; Update (replace) → PUT; Delete → DELETE

questions.stem: A script calling a controller API receives HTTP 401. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized = authentication needed or failed; 403 Forbidden = authenticated but not allowed.
options: The requested resource does not exist
The server hit an internal error
questions.whyCorrect: 401 means not authenticated.
whyWrong: That is 404.
That is 500.
Success codes are 2xx.

questions.stem: Which HTTP status code indicates that a POST request successfully created a new resource?
questions.explanation: 2xx = success, 4xx = client error, 5xx = server error.
questions.whyCorrect: The resource was created, often with its location returned.
whyWrong: 200 is generic success, typically for GET.
204 is success with no response body.
400 is a client error.

questions.stem: Which statements describe REST APIs? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: REST constraints: client-server, stateless, cacheable, uniform interface, layered system (and optional code-on-demand).
options: They are stateless; each request carries all the information the server needs
They use HTTP methods on resources identified by URIs
They require SNMP as the transport
They keep a session state on the server between calls
questions.whyCorrect: The server keeps no client session state between calls. For example, GET /api/v1/devices.
whyWrong: REST normally uses HTTP/HTTPS.
That would violate the stateless constraint.
JSON is the most common format; XML and YAML are also possible.

questions.stem: How many JSON objects does this document contain, including the outermost one?
questions.explanation: Every { } is an object; [ ] is an array. Count braces, not keys.
questions.whyCorrect: The outer object, the 'device' object and the two interface objects inside the array.
whyWrong: This misses one of the objects.
This counts only the outer and 'device' objects.
The array itself is not an object.

questions.stem: Which statement about this JSON document is correct?
questions.explanation: JSON value types: string, number, boolean, null, object and array.
options: 'interfaces' is an array containing two objects
questions.whyCorrect: Square brackets hold two { } objects.
whyWrong: true and false are unquoted JSON booleans.
"SW1" is a string.
There is only one array ('interfaces').

questions.stem: Which of these is valid JSON?
questions.explanation: JSON rules: double-quoted keys and strings, commas between members, no trailing commas, no comments.
questions.whyCorrect: Keys and strings use double quotes, and numbers are unquoted.
whyWrong: JSON does not allow single quotes.
Trailing commas are not allowed.
Keys must be quoted strings.

questions.stem: Which statements about Ansible are true? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Ansible key files: inventory (hosts and groups), playbooks (YAML), modules (units of work). It is written in Python and push-based.
options: It is agentless and connects to devices over SSH or APIs
It requires an agent on every managed device
questions.whyCorrect: No software is installed on managed devices. Plays and tasks are defined in YAML files.
whyWrong: That describes Puppet or Chef.
HCL is Terraform's language.

questions.stem: Which tool uses declarative HCL configuration files and keeps a state file of the resources it manages?
questions.explanation: Terraform is infrastructure as code: providers, plan/apply workflow, state file.
questions.whyCorrect: Terraform compares desired state in .tf files with its state file and applies the differences.
whyWrong: Ansible uses YAML playbooks and has no state file.
NETCONF is a device configuration protocol.
Syslog collects log messages.

questions.stem: Arrange the typical Terraform workflow steps in order.
questions.explanation: 'init' downloads providers, 'plan' previews changes, and 'apply' makes them.
questions.whyCorrect: Write the .tf configuration files → Run terraform init → Run terraform plan → Run terraform apply

questions.stem: Which Ansible file lists the managed devices and organizes them into groups?
questions.explanation: Example: an inventory group [access_switches] targeted by a playbook that sets NTP and banners.
questions.whyCorrect: The inventory defines hosts, groups and host variables.
whyWrong: A playbook defines the tasks to run.
A module is a unit of work called by a task.
State files belong to Terraform.

questions.stem: True or false: 'terraform plan' changes the managed infrastructure.
questions.explanation: 'terraform plan' only previews the changes Terraform would make; 'terraform apply' performs them.
questions.whyCorrect: The statement is false. 'terraform plan' only previews the changes Terraform would make; 'terraform apply' performs them.
whyWrong: The statement is false, so this choice is incorrect.

questions.stem: Which HTTP request header commonly carries a token for REST API authentication?
questions.explanation: Some APIs use custom headers (Catalyst Center uses X-Auth-Token), but the idea is the same: credentials accompany each request.
questions.whyCorrect: Token-based APIs expect the token on every stateless request.
whyWrong: Content-Type describes the body format, such as application/json.
Accept states which response formats the client can handle.
User-Agent identifies the client software.

questions.stem: Which statement best compares traditional and controller-based network management?
questions.explanation: Controllers add a central point for policy, automation, assurance and APIs.
options: Traditional is per-device; controller-based is centralized policy
Traditional networks have no control plane
Controller-based networks do not use IP addressing
questions.whyCorrect: The key difference is where control and intent live.
whyWrong: Every traditional device runs its own control plane.
IP is still used everywhere.
SNMP, syslog and similar tools work on traditional networks.
